Surah 103, Al-Asr (The Declining Day). Meccan, and its verses number 3. "Revealed after Al-Sharh."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

He swears by the prayer of Asr (the afternoon prayer) because of its excellence, as evidenced by the words of the Exalted: ﴿And the middle prayer﴾ [Qur'an 2:238], which is the Asr prayer, as it appears in the codex of Hafsah. And by the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever misses the Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth" [agreed upon (Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. And because the obligation in performing it is more arduous, since people are preoccupied with their trade and their gains at the end of the day, and busy with their livelihoods.

Or He swears by the evening, just as He swore by the morning (duha), because both contain signs of divine power. Or He swears by time, because in its passing are various kinds of wonders. "Man" (al-insan) is generic. "Loss" (al-khusr) means ruin (al-khusran), as it has been said: "Disbelief is in ingratitude (al-kufr fi al-kufran)." The meaning: people are in loss in their trade, except for the righteous alone, because they have bought the Hereafter with the world, so they profited and were made happy; while everyone else traded contrary to their trade, and so fell into ruin and wretchedness. ﴿And enjoin one another to truth﴾: to the established matter that cannot justly be denied, which is all good: from the affirmation of Allah's oneness and obedience to Him, following His books and messengers, abstaining from the world, and longing for the Hereafter. ﴿And enjoin one another to patience﴾: patience in refraining from sins and in performing acts of obedience, and in what Allah tests His servants with.

From the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever recites the surah Wal-Asr, Allah will forgive him, and he will be among those who enjoin one another to truth and enjoin one another to patience" [narrated by al-Tha'labi, al-Wahidi and Ibn Mardawayh with a chain going back to Ubayy ibn Ka'b].
